news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Raised to "Strong-Buy" at Chardan Capital
news.summary: Chardan Capital upgraded Lexeo Therapeutics to a Strong-Buy rating, joining a broadly bullish sell-side picture that also includes Oppenheimer's reiterated Outperform/$20 price target following the HEROIC-PKP2 interim data. The upgrade contrasts with Weiss Ratings, which continues to rate the stock Sell despite nudging its internal grade up slightly in mid-July.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics CEO, CFO and COO Sell Shares to Cover RSU Tax Withholding
news.summary: On July 1, 2026, CEO Nolan Townsend sold 25,947 shares, CFO Louis Tamayo sold 4,641 shares, and COO Jose Manuel Otero sold 4,666 shares, all at roughly $4.48-$4.49, in routine pre-scheduled transactions to cover tax withholding on RSUs that vested on June 29. None of the sales were discretionary open-market trades.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics CEO and CFO Receive Restricted Stock Unit Awards
news.summary: CEO Nolan Townsend was granted 67,000 restricted stock units as part of his compensation package, with CFO Louis Tamayo receiving a smaller 12,000-unit award on the same date, June 29, 2026.

news.headline: JPMorgan Cuts Lexeo Therapeutics Price Target to $9 from $12, Maintains Overweight
news.summary: JPMorgan trimmed its LXEO price target to $9 from $12 while reiterating an Overweight rating, citing an updated valuation model following recent pipeline developments; the cut came the same day the company held its virtual annual meeting and elected three directors.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Announces Publication in JAMA Cardiology of Phase I/II Data for LX2006 in Friedreich Ataxia
news.summary: Peer-reviewed Phase I/II data on 17 Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy patients treated with LX2006 showed sustained cardiac and neurologic improvements, favorable biomarker changes, and a generally well-tolerated safety profile, reinforcing the clinical rationale behind the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 program.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Announces Regulatory Update and Registrational Trial Design for LX2006 Gene Therapy in Friedreich Ataxia
news.summary: Lexeo finalized with the FDA the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial protocol and statistical analysis plan for LX2006, confirmed it can use its optimized Sf9-baculovirus commercial-scale manufacturing process for dosing, and targeted a BLA submission under the accelerated approval pathway in H1 2028; enrollment of the first patient was expected by end of June 2026, and shares jumped nearly 13% on the news.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: Lexeo is expected to report second-quarter 2026 financial results and pipeline updates in August 2026 (it reported Q2 2025 results on August 14, 2025); an exact 2026 date has not yet been announced.

catalysts.label: LX2020 12-month high-dose data (HEROIC-PKP2)
catalysts.detail: Company guidance calls for a 12-month data update covering all high-dose PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy participants in the ongoing HEROIC-PKP2 Phase I/II trial.

catalysts.label: SUNRISE-FA2 topline data readout
catalysts.detail: Topline data from the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial of LX2006 in Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy is guided for the second half of 2027.

catalysts.label: LX2006 BLA submission
catalysts.detail: Lexeo plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the FDA for LX2006 under the accelerated approval pathway in the first half of 2028.

catalysts.label: First patient dosed in pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial
catalysts.detail: Following the June 2026 FDA-aligned trial design finalization, Lexeo guided to enrolling the first SUNRISE-FA2 pivotal-trial participant by the end of June 2026; as of late July 2026 no separate press release confirming actual first dosing had been issued.

pulse: Lexeo remains a clinical-stage cardiovascular gene therapy company advancing two lead AAV programs, LX2006 for Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy and LX2020 for PKP2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, having finalized the FDA-aligned SUNRISE-FA2 pivotal trial design in mid-June 2026 (sending shares up nearly 13%) and followed that with supportive LX2006 data published in JAMA Cardiology days later. Since then, company-specific news has been quiet and dominated by routine insider RSU grants and tax-related sales by the CEO, CFO and COO, while sell-side sentiment has stayed mixed-to-positive: JPMorgan trimmed its price target to $9 (from $12, still Overweight) in late June, Oppenheimer holds an Outperform/$20 target, and Chardan Capital raised its rating to Strong-Buy in late July even as Weiss Ratings continues to rate the stock a Sell. The shares have traded rangebound in the mid-single digits (roughly $4.50-$5.50) through late July after falling sharply from a 52-week high near $11. With cash guided to last into 2028 (following a workforce reduction earlier in 2026 to focus resources on the cardiac pipeline), the next concrete catalysts are Q2 2026 earnings expected in August, confirmation of first-patient dosing in SUNRISE-FA2, 12-month high-dose LX2020 data in Q4 2026, and SUNRISE-FA2 topline data in H2 2027 ahead of a planned 2028 BLA filing.
